definitions.explanation: A traffic accident in which only property (vehicles, structures, etc.) is damaged and no person is injured. Contrasted with {人身事故|じんしんじこ} (personal injury accident). Important in insurance and legal contexts.

examples.japanese: {幸|さいわ}い{物損事故|ぶっそんじこ}で{済|す}んだ。
examples.english: Fortunately, it was only a property damage accident.

examples.japanese: {物損事故|ぶっそんじこ}でも{警察|けいさつ}に{届|とど}けるべきだ。
examples.english: Even for a property damage accident, you should report it to the police.

examples.japanese: {駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}で{物損事故|ぶっそんじこ}を{起|お}こしたが、{相手|あいて}の{車|くるま}の{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}が{見|み}つからなかった。
examples.english: I caused a property damage accident in the parking lot, but I couldn't find the owner of the other car.

notes:
USAGE:
A legal and insurance term frequently encountered in daily life. In Japan, even minor fender benders should be reported to the police for insurance purposes. A {物損事故|ぶっそんじこ} has different legal and insurance implications than a {人身事故|じんしんじこ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {物損事故|ぶっそんじこ}を{起|お}こす (to cause a property damage accident)
- {物損事故|ぶっそんじこ}で{済|す}む (to end up as just property damage)
- {物損事故|ぶっそんじこ}の{届|とど}け{出|で} (reporting a property damage accident)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {人身事故|じんしんじこ}: personal injury accident — an accident involving injuries to people
- {交通事故|こうつうじこ}: traffic accident — the general term covering all types
